corpus_role: WHAT THIS CORPUS IS, AND IS NOT (recorded 2026-09-02 after getting it wrong twice in one day). It is a CHANGE DETECTOR: it compares melange against melange, so a deck's circuit quality is irrelevant to catching a refactor that moves output. It is NOT an ACCURACY ORACLE. 44 of the pre-prune 46 decks were unstable/ tier and stable/ is empty, so almost every deck is an in-progress or abandoned circuit. NEVER cite a render from these decks as evidence about a circuit, about which solver path is more correct, or about audible behaviour — 'rigour applied to a broken ruler produces confident wrong conclusions, not safe ones' (oomox user, 2026-08-16). Note the asymmetry that makes the corpus still useful: AGREEMENT is robust to deck quality (a bad circuit cannot manufacture agreement between two implementations), DISAGREEMENT is not (it cannot separate 'the code differs' from 'this circuit is pathological'). A broken deck may DETECT a defect; it can never BE the evidence for one. Adjudicating accuracy requires ngspice, on a completed deck.
